result.description: Fires on function words (' of', ' in', ' is', ' and') right after the word "diversity" or "diversification", where the next word is likely a category like species, inclusion or populations. Silent on ' of' after other nouns such as levels or impact.
result.label: Function word after "diversity"

result.description: Fires on mechanical/engineering modifier nouns like " driver", " motor", " gauge" when they come right after a modifier or word and precede another noun (driver control, motor vehicles, motor neurons). Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: driver/motor/gauge noun modifiers

result.description: Fires on contraction suffixes 've' and 're' right after "you'" (e.g. "you've ever", "next time you're"), predicting a following verb. Members detect 've' tokens and apostrophes.
result.label: you've / you're contraction suffix

result.description: Fires on the first piece of an uppercase acronym being spelled out, mainly ' ER' (ERP) and ' SD' (SDN), where more letters follow. Members detect acronym fragments such as SD, CD, UI and ER.
result.label: Acronym-initial letters (ER/SD)

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece "itory" in "auditory" (also " wet", " bitter", " wheel" at lower counts). Members are mainly "itory"/auditory detectors. Stays silent in a nearby passage about motor skills that lacks the word.
result.label: "itory" in auditory

result.description: Fires on mixed connector or boundary tokens such as " or", " (", "/", "0" and " and", often after a list item or number. It stays quiet on " or" between some noun pairs. The evidence is mixed and the members are mostly generic.
result.label: Mixed connectors: or, parenthesis, slash

result.description: Fires on connectives (' and', ' for', ' of') right after the word "standards" (e.g. "standards and certifications", "standards for quality"), where a quality or certification term comes next. Silent on 'and' after other nouns like food or accuracy.
result.label: Connective after "standards"

result.description: Fires on art-medium and technique words (painting, paint, engraving, negative spaces, animation) in text about visual art techniques. Members detect art-related tokens like gesso, glazing, colors, impasto, printmaking terms.
result.label: Visual art technique nouns
Cold War topic words
result.description: Fires on varied tokens within Cold War / arms race text (Space Race, rivalry, nuclear, stability, implications). Members detect Cold, War, Soviet Union, arms. It stays silent on 'arms' in other war contexts.

Weak, scattered target firing on nouns and quantifiers after "all/other" in game-theory or market contexts (players, participants, all, their, sessions). Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered group-noun slots (unclear)
'bit' in Arbitrage
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'bit' inside "Arbitrage" (mainly "Arbitrage Pricing" at document start). The 'bit' in "orbit/orbitals" is covered by members but the target is silent in the contrast. Predicts the continuation 'rage'.
Fires on the pieces of the surname "Galvani" (' Gal' and 'v') after the first name Luigi. Stays silent on 'v' in "Galvani" without Luigi before it, so it seems to need the first-name context.
result.label: Luigi Galvani name pieces

result.description: Fires on the word " present" (the present tense, "the present", "present relevance") in English grammar and tense explanations. It was silent on a bare "present" opening a list of tenses. Members detect "present" and nearby grammar words.
result.label: "present" in tense grammar text

result.description: Fires in text about converting or translating one form into another (convert, converting, translating, conversion), including tokens inside such a clause. Silent on 'ating' in other verbs like facilitating or navigating. Predicts ' into'.
result.label: Convert/translate into another form

result.description: Fires on scattered, unrelated tokens (word pieces like 'us', ' make', ' (', ' times', ' and') with no common meaning. Members are generic token detectors across layers 0-3. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token attention latent

result.description: Fires on the start or middle of a word piece (per-, mult-, intr-, -icate) that follows "complex and", where the adjective being begun is a synonym like perplexing, multifaceted or intricate. Silent on "intr" in other phrasings.
result.label: Word pieces after "complex and"

result.description: Fires on the continuation piece after "germ" (mostly "ination", also "pl" in germplasm, "cells", "theory of"), in biology text. Members include several detectors of the " germ" token.
result.label: Word pieces following "germ"

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-phrase tokens (word endings like 'ra', 'etic', opening quotes or parentheses, conjunctions like 'or') in expository text. No dominant token or clear shared context; peak consistency is low and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on " preceding" as a modifier in "the sum of the two preceding ones" (Fibonacci-style definitions). Members detect similar relational/positional modifiers like before, past, previous, original, existing, surrounding.
result.label: " preceding" in "two preceding ones"

result.description: Fires on word pieces following "Strategic" or "strategic" (e.g. Compet-, Position-ing, Risk, Innovation, planning, strategies), in business-strategy headings. Silent on 'ative' in narrative or imaginative text. Members detect strateg- pieces.
result.label: Tokens after "strategic" in business

result.description: Fires on "the" and "other" inside the idiom "on the other hand", peaking on "other" or the preceding "the". It stays silent on "other" in ordinary uses such as "each other" or "many other".
result.label: "on the other hand" idiom

result.description: Fires on "ancient" (' ancient' or the 'cient' piece of "Ancient") in text about ancient civilizations such as Greece, Rome, Babylon and Mesopotamia. Members detect 'cient' and ' ancient' tokens plus Mesopotamia and Sumer terms. It is silent on unrelated text.
result.label: "Ancient" in ancient-civilization text

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'pp' and 'os' in "Opposite" (also 'Doppler', 'rejects'), in philosophy/theory-style text. Evidence is thin and mixed; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Mid-word 'pp'/'os' pieces in Opposite

result.description: Fires on the linking verb ' are' (also ' is', ' were') when it begins a sentence or follows a fragment with the subject missing or cut off, as in "principles are applied". It stays silent when a full subject noun phrase precedes it.
result.label: Copula after truncated subject

result.description: Fires on the word "impact" and tokens that follow or continue it (impact+s, assessments, "on", possessive 's), in text about the effects of one thing on another. Members are mostly impact/effects/affect detectors.
result.label: impact/effects word and its continuations

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' of', ' become', 'ax', ' its', ' we') in historical or era-describing prose near the start of a document, such as "period of", "climax of". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in era-description prose

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments (e.g. 'ular', 'u', ' C', 'ating') inside long or garbled technical or title-case words, where the word is unfinished. Evidence is weak and mixed; the circuit failed faithfulness and its members are generic.
result.label: Mid-word fragments in technical titles

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (" in", " construction", " operation", " of", " its") that follow an abstract topic noun in explanatory text, where a noun phrase about how something works or is built is being continued. The peak token is inconsistent and the evidence is thin.
result.label: Process-noun continuation in explanatory text

result.description: Fires on a present-tense transitive verb (enable, provide, modify, shape, define) right after a plural or abstract subject noun, where an object is expected next. Silent on 'enable' after relative 'that' or 'also'. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Main verb after noun subject

result.description: Fires on 'fair' and the token completing a "fair ..." word (fair trade, fair trad-ed, fairness, fair wages). Needs a preceding 'fair'; 'ness' in weakness or consciousness stays silent.
result.label: Fair + trade/ness completion

result.description: Fires on ' time' mainly in "the same time" (also "constant time", "each time zone"). Silent on "At the same time" at sentence start and on other uses like "a time when", so it seems to need a particular construction or position.
result.label: ' time' after "the same"

result.description: Peaks are scattered across mid-word pieces ('ct', 'Electron'), conjunctions, commas and 's'. It is silent on 's' in name lists such as "Dr. Daniels.". The circuit is diffuse and failed, so no clear pattern emerges.
result.label: Diffuse mixed tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on the preposition or word right after "signed" in treaty text (e.g. "signed on June…", "signed soon after"), where a date is expected. It stays silent on " in" after other verbs like "established in" or "involved in".
result.label: Word after "signed" in treaties

result.description: Fires on ' and' in the fixed binomial "ebb and flow" (right after "ebb"). It stays silent on ordinary ' and' joining other words or clauses.
result.label: 'and' in "ebb and flow"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' the', ' robust', ' total', 'ity', ' original') that follow verbs like ensure, maintain, predict, preserve. The circuit is weak and diffuse, with no clear discriminative members, and it stays silent on many ' the' cases.
result.label: Object slot after maintain/ensure verbs

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-phrase tokens (e.g. 'ation', ' regional', ' Ulrich', ' voting') in abstract academic prose. No dominant token, and it is silent on 'ation' in 'innovation' in some contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Scattered academic mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on the "t" of imperative "don't" (don't worry, don't fight) at the start of a sentence, giving advice or commands. Silent on "doesn't" or "don't have to" in descriptive statements. Weaker on "get", "to", "need" in similar directive contexts.
result.label: Imperative "don't" at sentence start

result.description: Fires on the copula (' is', ' are', ' be') right after a short abstract noun-phrase subject near the start of a document, such as "Effective techniques are" or "Accurate data is", where an evaluative adjective like essential or crucial is expected. Silent after pronouns or mid-sentence subjects.
result.label: Copula after abstract subject phrase

result.description: Fires on the noun ' examples' (also ' example', ' studies', ' instance') when it is being introduced as illustrative material, e.g. "several successful examples", "provide examples of", "case studies". Members detect example/case-study words.
result.label: ' examples' noun introducing illustrations

result.description: Fires weakly on varied nouns or word pieces (system, data, social, time) that end a technical or academic noun-phrase modifier, often just before a head noun. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is low-faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Academic compound-noun modifier tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-word pieces and tokens in academic or scientific text (e.g. 'ations', 'ib', '-', ' framework'). Peaks are inconsistent, and it is silent on 'ations' in some contexts. Circuit failed and looks diffuse.
result.label: Scattered academic word-piece fragments

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (performances, music, through, quote marks, 'and') in music licensing and copyright text, where the next word is likely a music or rights term such as records or claims. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Music licensing text, mixed tokens

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-latent peaking on scattered tokens: 'O' in "CEO", ' for', ' from', 'ing', ' in'. Members are generic word-piece detectors with no discriminative signal, and the contrast shows 'O' silent in similar CEO contexts. Evidence is too thin to say more.
result.label: Scattered tokens, CEO 'O' and prepositions

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied tokens (and, of, that, cost, RAM) in technical expository text about computing and engineering, often mid-list or after a noun. Evidence is mixed; the circuit is unfaithful and its members are generic.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical text

result.description: Fires on ' solar' (and 'els' in "solar panels", ' cells', ' wind') in renewable-energy text, mostly where solar is a modifier before power/panels/energy. Silent on general renewable-energy text without solar. Members detect solar and energy words.
result.label: solar energy term in renewable text

result.description: Fires on 'on' (also 'os') right after the 'pp' piece at the start of a sentence, as in "pp|on|ents" (proponents) or "pp|os|crats", where a word is split into fragments. It is silent on ordinary text.
result.label: 'on' after 'pp' word-piece

result.description: Fires on markup and LaTeX symbol tokens such as '|', long dash runs, backslashes and '{', often at or near the start of a document or in code/math-like formatting. Silent on ordinary prose.
result.label: Markup and LaTeX symbol tokens

result.description: Fires on ' with', ' sentence', ' paragraph' right after "concluding"/"closing" in descriptions of essay or story structure (concluding sentence, concluding with). Silent on ordinary "with" elsewhere. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Concluding/closing sentence or 'with'

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit. Peaks mostly on ' brought' after a subject like "digital revolution also", with stray hits on ' on' and ' father'. Members are generic token detectors and don't explain it well. The target is silent on ' brought' after "postmodern era".
result.label: ' brought' after abstract subject (weak)

result.description: Fires on the verb ' is' (sometimes ' are'/' was') right after a defined term with its acronym in parentheses, e.g. "Systems Engineering (SE) is", at the start of a document. It stays quiet on plain topic subjects without an acronym.
result.label: ' is' after parenthesized acronym

result.description: Fires on the word or punctuation right after "vegetation" or "vegetative" (cover, comma, and) in ecology and soil text. It stays quiet on ordinary "and" in other ecology lists. Logits are mixed.
result.label: Token after vegetation in ecology

result.description: Fires on word pieces following "Organ" (iz, om, ol, omet), i.e. mid-word continuations of words starting with "Organ", such as "Organizational" and "Organomagnesia". It also fires weakly on " Organ" itself. It is silent on ordinary heading text.
result.label: Organ- word continuation pieces

result.description: Fires on ' hand' in the contrastive phrase "on the other hand", relying on the preceding "the other" and "on". Silent on unrelated text lacking this phrase.
result.label: "hand" in "on the other hand"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and predicates (of, with, less, they, have, feature) in technical or scientific expository text, mostly where a descriptive property or complement follows. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on word pieces that continue a word beginning with "Del"/"del" (Delacroix, Delayed, Delineation, delight, delicate), on the token after "Del". Members detect " Del" and mid-word pieces like ac/ic.
result.label: Word pieces after "Del"

result.description: Diffuse attention latent firing on scattered tokens in abstract or academic prose (' manifest', '-ity' suffixes, ' and', en dash, mid-word pieces). No single token dominates; the evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Diffuse academic-prose mixed tokens

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ' for', ' of', 'ent', ' up', ' to') mid-phrase in expository text. Peaks are inconsistent, members are generic token detectors, and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function-word and fragment peaks

result.description: Fires on varied tokens, often the end of a modifier or noun in an adjective-noun phrase (e.g. "cultural context", "fiscal policies", "multifaceted"), where a list item or conjunction could follow. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered phrase-final noun/modifier positions

result.description: Fires on ' other' as a determiner in a list or addition ("X, Y, and other similar Z", "or other"), preceded by and/or/as well as. Silent on "other than", "each other", and "touches on other".
result.label: "and/or other" list continuation

result.description: Fires on the letters "P"/"PP" in the abbreviation PPP (public-private partnership), mainly the second or third P. It stays quiet on P in other acronyms such as UNDP. Members detect single P tokens.
result.label: P in PPP abbreviation

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in technical or scientific text (' to', digits, commas, ' is', word pieces) with no clear shared token or construction. Consistency is low and the members are mostly word-piece detectors. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered technical-text tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on words about writing systems (' characters', ' script', 'etic' in alphabetic/phonetic, ' sounds') in text comparing scripts and alphabets. Members detect script/alphabet words and linguistics terms.
result.label: Writing systems and scripts terms

result.description: Fires on the "inos" piece inside "luminosity" (mostly in astrophysics text about stars), occasionally on other word endings like "ence" or "ity". Members include detectors of "inos" and star/astronomy context.
result.label: "inos" in luminosity

result.description: Fires on commas (and some ' is'/' was') that end a subject noun phrase or clause in expository text, where a continuation like "which", "including" or a verb follows. Silent on many similar commas, so the extra condition is unclear.
result.label: Clause-ending commas in expository prose

result.description: Fires on varied tokens inside list-like items, especially topic or heading entries in lists of terms (e.g. "Truth Tables", "Logical Connectives", "Articles"). Peaks are mixed word pieces and commas; the evidence is weak and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: List item word pieces in term lists

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' the', 'using', ' Graphics', ' experiments') in academic or science text. No consistent token or context; the circuit is mostly generic token-level hubs, and the contrast does not clarify the condition.
result.label: Scattered academic-text tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on word-final pieces or suffix-like tokens completing a compound or technical noun (Babb-age, Environment-al, behavior-ists, Sketch-pad), plus nouns like cycle or control. Peaks are diverse and the circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: Word-ending suffix pieces in compounds

result.description: Fires on the word piece completing a noun after "main" or "primary" (e.g. "main ingredient", "primary antibodies", "central role"). It is silent in general flavor text without that modifier. Peaks are scattered across pieces like ing, red, ient.
result.label: Noun after main/primary modifier

result.description: Fires on tokens right after the word "soft" (a hyphen, "br", " ones", " reality", " skin", " g"), where the next piece continues a soft-compound. Members detect "soft", "-ness", "-ening". Silent on hyphens after other words.
result.label: Token following "soft"

result.description: Fires on the token after "engagement" (strateg-ies, metrics, at, by) in workplace/marketing text. Silent on "strategies" after other words like employer-led or computational, so it needs the preceding "engagement".
result.label: Word after "engagement"

result.description: Fires on " space"/" spaces" when it follows "metric" (mathematical topology context). It stays silent on "space" after other words like "different", "Y-axis" or in "space geometry".
result.label: "space" after "metric"

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' al' when it starts a longer word (aldehyde, altruism, alloy, alliance, alphabetic), predicting a continuation like 'loy' or 'ike'. Silent on the contrast text, which has no ' al' token.
result.label: ' al' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on a preposition or conjunction (mostly " into", also " in"/" and") right after the word "humor", as in "integrating humor into". It stays quiet on " into" after "insight(s)" or "data".
result.label: Preposition right after "humor"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, often apostrophes, 's', ' in', ' your', or word endings in academic text. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is weak. It stays silent on possessive apostrophes after plural nouns.
result.label: Scattered apostrophe and function tokens

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside the prefix "supra-" words, mainly "suprachiasmatic" (rach, ias) and "supraglacial" (rag), also weakly in "superposition". Needs the rare word-piece sequence after "sup".
result.label: sup-rach-ias / supra word pieces

result.description: Fires on name pieces (first names, middle or surname fragments like ' von', ' L', 'es') inside a full person name after a scientist or historian title or first name, where a surname continues. Circuit evidence is diffuse and weak.
result.label: Mid-name pieces of scientist names

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens such as 'ring' in "stirring", ' bond' in "bonding", and sometimes ' the' or ' and', mostly in science or math text. Evidence is thin and scattered; the circuit failed faithfulness and has no clear shared trigger.
result.label: Scattered science word pieces (ring, bond)

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target firing on varied function words (' and', ' in', ' with', ' than') and occasional nouns mid-sentence. Peaks are inconsistent, the contrast silences ' and' too, and members are generic token detectors, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered function words, unclear

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (nouns, commas, word pieces) in dense expository academic or technical prose, often mid-list or after a noun phrase. Peaks are scattered and the circuit failed, so the evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: Scattered expository-prose tokens, weak circuit

result.description: Fires on capitalized word-initial pieces, most often ' Man' in literary conflict lists ("Man vs. Self", "Man vs. Nature"), also Mon, Ch, Self. Mixed weaker cases on name fragments. Evidence is thin and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Man in "Man vs." conflict lists

result.description: Fires on the 's' of "It's" (contraction after "It" starting a sentence), also weakly on " is" or "They" in similar sentence-initial slots. Silent on possessive 's and other 's contractions.
result.label: Sentence-initial "It's" contraction

result.description: Fires on ' least' in "at least" and on tokens shortly after it (the quantity or date that follows, e.g. "at least 2 scholars", "at least the 2020s"). Members are mostly "at least" detectors, so it tracks the phrase's scope.
result.label: "at least" phrase and its scope

result.description: Fires on ' its' (also 'their', 'ability') right after a sentence-initial preposition like "Through its" or "With its" or "Despite its", opening a descriptive phrase. Silent on ' its' mid-sentence after verbs or prepositions like "in its" or "beyond its".
result.label: Sentence-initial "Through/With its" possessive

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas in lists of abstract nouns, "their", word pieces) in expository, business or academic text, often within lists or titles. Peaks are scattered and contrast shows no clear condition. Evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: Scattered list and title tokens

result.description: Fires on " moving" (rarely " move") especially as a participial phrase after a comma, continuing a sentence ("..., moving towards/through/on to"). Members detect move/moving/pushing tokens and -ing forms.
result.label: Participial " moving" after comma

result.description: Fires on the 's' of a possessive after an apostrophe following a noun or name (Queen's, Fermat's, moment's). Silent on contraction "it's"/"let's" and verb-ending -s.
result.label: Possessive 's after nouns

result.description: Fires on ' matter' in "dark matter" and on "gravit-ational" in cosmology/physics text about dark matter. It stays quiet on ' matter' in other uses (matter and radiation, state of matter), so it needs the dark-matter/cosmology context.
result.label: Dark matter / gravitational in cosmology

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (verbs like 'presents', prepositions, possessive endings, word fragments) inside abstract academic or technical prose, often just before a noun phrase. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered tokens in academic prose

result.description: Fires on words following "emphasizes" (the, importance, practical) in sentences where a subject such as an approach or philosophy "emphasizes" something. Members detect emphasize/emphasis tokens earlier in the sentence. Silent on "importance" after "emphasizing"/"highlights".
result.label: Object slot after "emphasizes"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens, most often the suffix "an" in "Minoan" (ancient-culture adjectives), also " and", " networks" and fragments of capitalized names. Silent on "an" in Canaan and Nabataean. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Minoan 'an' and scattered tokens

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on ' allocation' after "such as task", plus word pieces like 'ified', 'ict', and 'called' in "so-called". Silent on "resource allocation" in the contrast. Circuit failed; members are generic.
result.label: Mixed: 'task allocation' and word pieces

result.description: Fires on varied words in math/linear-algebra text, often a noun or function word right after "and" or "that" (e.g. "and its", "and columns", "that are", "vectors"). Weak, mixed evidence; the circuit failed and its members are generic.
result.label: Math text word after 'and'/'that'

result.description: Fires on ' that' as a complementizer right after a verb of proposing, arguing, stating or showing (proposed that, argued that, states that), especially in scientific or philosophical claims. Silent on relative-clause 'that' after nouns.
result.label: complementizer 'that' after claim verbs

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in academic or technical prose: prepositions like ' for', ' in', ' from', and mid-word pieces. The pattern is diffuse and the contrast shows ' for' staying silent in some contexts. The evidence is too mixed for a clear condition.
result.label: Diffuse prepositions and word pieces

result.description: Fires mostly on commas inside lists of abstract nouns (e.g. "individual rights, civil liberties, political freedom"), plus scattered tokens like ' responses' and word endings. It stays quiet on commas in other contexts. Weak, mixed circuit.
result.label: Commas in abstract noun lists

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces and nouns (opol, ential, changes, dis) inside lists of political, economic and environmental risk factors, such as instability, policy changes, geopolitical context. Peaks are scattered. The contrast 'oligopolistic' stays silent.
result.label: Risk-factor lists in economic/political text

result.description: Fires on the word " bronze" in discussions of metals and materials, mostly as a subject-like noun after "with", "like" or a comma. It is silent on some bronze tokens after "or", "of", "on" or "particularly". Upstream members detect iron, metal, stone and ancient-civilization words.
result.label: bronze in metals/materials text

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ible' in "tangible" and on ' and' right after "tangible" (heading toward "intangible"). It stays silent on ' and' in other contexts like "cost and quality". Members mostly detect tang-/ible pieces and physical/concrete words.
result.label: tangible: 'ible' and following 'and'

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in mid-list or coordinated positions in technical or expository text, mostly ' and', ' or', and noun pieces, where a further item or continuation follows. It stays silent on many ' and' tokens, and the circuit's members are diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse coordination/list continuation token

result.description: Fires diffusely on function words and word endings (commas, " of", " to", " and") in abstract, generic academic or essay prose, mid-phrase. The peak token is mixed and the contrast is silent on commas, so the condition is not clear.
result.label: Diffuse function words in abstract prose

result.description: Fires weakly on function words (' of', ' these', ' like', ' a', ' among') inside academic or explanatory prose, where the next word is a noun phrase. It stays silent on many ' of' tokens in "noun of" phrases, and the circuit fails to explain why.
result.label: Function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the word " here" (also " Here"), mostly in "it's here", "will be here", or "X here is..." where it refers to presence or the present context. Members are mostly detectors of " here" itself.
result.label: ' here' token detector

result.description: Fires on the prefix ' over' after "tendency to" (as in overfit, overuse), where it begins a word. It stays quiet on 'over' in other words like overcoming, overlooked, overload. Circuit is weak and mostly generic.
result.label: 'over' prefix after "tendency to"

result.description: Fires mostly on ' of' (also 'and', 'the', 'pper') in technical or academic prose, but stays silent on many ' of' in math contexts like "notion of" and "size of". Members are mostly math and science token detectors; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Selective ' of' in technical prose

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'ple' of "Princi-ple" when it completes a named principle, especially "Inclusion-Exclusion Principle". It is silent on 'ple' in other "Principle" contexts, such as "Pigeonhole Principle" or a bare "Principle".
result.label: 'ple' in Inclusion-Exclusion Principle

result.description: Fires on tokens in lists of "Biomedical X" course or field headings (Sensors, Optics, Control, micro-/Micro- in Biomedical Microelectronics), and on "applications" after biomedical/clinical. Silent on micro- in general science text.
result.label: Biomedical field heading words

result.description: Fires on the token right after "on" (research/work on ...), including ' the', a space, or a word start/piece like ' g', ' h', ' mole'. It marks the start of the topic of someone's work or research. Quiet after "on" in "Memoir on the".
result.label: Topic after "work/research on"

result.description: Fires on varied verb endings and function words (-ing, evaluate, their, address) in marketing/communication text about tailoring messages to audiences, often just before "their". Inconsistent; silent on some -ing tokens (crafting, aligning).
result.label: Audience-messaging verbs before 'their'

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces of proper names and rare words (liance, ien, ine, -ione, -RI-) in history, science and European-name text. Peaks are scattered, and the circuit fails faithfulness, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Mid-word pieces of names

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens (' is', ' to', ' and', word pieces) in list-like or abstract expository text. Members are list items and word-piece detectors; the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in lists

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (' each', ' of', ' that', 'able', ' for') in expository text, with no consistent token. Members are generic and non-specific, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered function-word attention latent

result.description: Fires mainly on ' to' as an infinitive marker of purpose after a subject using or applying something ("agencies use these rules to assess", "utilize them to determine"), also on 'used' and 'use'. Silent on other 'to' uses, e.g. after artists or related to.
result.label: Purpose 'to' after use/utilize

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (word pieces, 's', function words, nouns) mid-word or mid-phrase in technical or academic text. No consistent token or context; members are generic token detectors. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token attention latent

result.description: Fires on varied words (guide, beauty, communication, -ics) in creative or artistic writing about art, music, stories and emotion, where the next word is likely an artistic or creative verb or noun. Peaks are scattered and low in consistency.
result.label: Arts and creative-writing context words

result.description: Weak, diffuse attention latent firing on varied tokens (word endings like -ess, -ment, 'music', 'relations', ' the') in abstract academic text. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse abstract-academic word endings

result.description: Fires on ' Getting' as the first word of a new paragraph or document-initial sentence, a gerund subject opening. Members detect get/getting forms and -ing words; it is silent mid-sentence.
result.label: Sentence-initial "Getting"

result.description: Fires on ' work' (also research, contribution) right after a scientist's possessive name plus an adjective like "groundbreaking" or "seminal", i.e. a noun for scholarly output. Silent when work isn't attributed to a named person's possessive.
result.label: Scholar's groundbreaking 'work'

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (suffix 'ize', commas, 'with respect', 'among', 'under') in academic text, often about language. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse, with no discriminative members. 'ize' stays silent in some words.
result.label: Diffuse academic mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on ' Car' (also ' Rach', ' P') right after "Rachel", as the surname start of Rachel Carson. It stays silent on ' Car' after other first names (John Carmack, Thomas Carlyle, George Washington Carver).
result.label: Car in Rachel Carson

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' o' of oxygen, ' (', ' and') in lists of chemical or scientific items, e.g. element names with symbols. Weak, mixed evidence; silent on 'or oxygen' in a fluid context.
result.label: Science list items before next term

result.description: Fires on the piece "day" in "everyday" when used as an adjective before a noun (everyday life, conversations, problems). Members are mostly detectors of "day"/"daily" in earlier layers.
result.label: "day" in "everyday"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ert' in "tertiary" (after 't'), mostly in colour-related text. Weakly fires on similar mid-word pieces after t (tau, pluck). Members detect 'ert' and nearby word-start fragments like 'et' and 'ect'.
result.label: 'ert' in "tertiary"

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-word pieces and function words (sandstone, 'ic', 'na', ' in', ' the') in technical expository text, probably where a word or noun phrase is unfinished. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and low-faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mid-word pieces in expository text

result.description: Fires on " of" in the idiom "the grand/greater scheme of" (things, history, events). It stays silent on " of" after other nouns such as vastness, part, matter or branch.
result.label: " of" in "grand scheme of"

result.description: Fires on the token right after "ten" in words and compounds starting with "ten" (ten-, tenor, tenet, "ten dB"). Silent on hyphens after other number words like two-, six-. Members detect "ten" and "or".
result.label: Continuation after "ten" prefix

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens in finance, legal and marketing text (e.g. 'ities' in "Securities", ' of', ' Exchange'), but not on 'ities' in opportunities or realities. Evidence is mixed and the circuit's faithfulness is poor.
result.label: Finance/legal phrase-internal tokens

result.description: Fires on the last noun or item in a list of technical or abstract concepts (e.g. "corrosion resistance", "credit factors", "strategic planning"), often just before a comma or "and". Silent on ordinary clause-level commas. Evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: Final item in technical list

result.description: Weak, scattered circuit firing on varied tokens (' and', 'ical', ' period', ' food') mid-phrase in expository text. The peaks share no clear token or construction, and members are mostly generic token detectors. Circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase expository tokens

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ation' completing "deforestation" in environmental text. It stays silent on 'ation' in other words like degradation, transportation or overhunting.
result.label: 'ation' in "deforestation"

result.description: Fires on the "ys" ending of "valleys" (also "valley") in geology and landforms text, such as glacial valleys and mountains. It stays silent on "ys" in other words like "journeys".
result.label: valleys in geology text

result.description: Fires mostly on the verb "challenge" (and nearby tokens like "to", "'", "established") when writers, narratives or devices challenge readers' views or conventions, in literary/cultural-commentary text. Members are mostly "challenge" detectors.
result.label: Verb "challenge" in literary commentary

result.description: Fires on function tokens (' and', ' of', '-') right after a "digitization/digitizing/digitally" word, i.e. the word following a digit- stem. Silent on ' and' after other words. Members detect digit/ization and digital-art tokens.
result.label: ' and'/' of' after digitization

result.description: Fires on " than" (occasionally " more") in "nothing more than", the restrictive "only/merely" construction. It stays silent on "more than just" after other words. Members are negation and "nothing/no/else" detectors.
result.label: "nothing more than" than

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-word pieces and function words (os, as, ing, nature, its, imply) in expository text, mostly where a word or phrase is still incomplete. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so no clear pattern.
result.label: Scattered mid-word and function tokens

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on varied tokens (' to', ' and', word endings like 'ues', 'ics', 'ery') in technical or energy-related expository text, often ending a noun phrase. The circuit failed faithfulness; members are generic and non-discriminative.
result.label: Scattered tokens in technical expository text

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative " these" (also " These", "ese"), strongest when it begins a new clause after a comma or semicolon and refers back to a just-mentioned plural set. It is quieter after verbs or prepositions.
result.label: clause-initial "these" after punctuation

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (the, commas, word pieces, your) inside flowery "journey/adventure/voyage" prose, such as "embarking on a journey through...". Members detect journey/through words. It stays silent on "the" in ordinary non-journey text.
result.label: Journey-adventure prose, varied tokens

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe after a noun (artist', writer', chef') where a possessive "s" or similar suffix is expected. It stays quiet on some apostrophes, such as after "it" or in some plural possessives.
result.label: Possessive apostrophe after noun

result.description: Fires on the first word or word piece of an adjective or modifier right after "combination of" (sophistic-ated, intr-icate, met-iculous, technological). Members detect "combination/combined/combining" and "and/with/between" blending contexts.
result.label: Adjective after "combination of"

result.description: Fires on material names and word pieces in materials-science text, such as 'ium' in titanium, ' carbon' before fiber, and 'ural' in structural. Upstream members detect material, alloy, steel and fiber words. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: Materials-science material name pieces

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in technical or scientific prose, such as plural suffixes (-ases, -ities, -ations), mid-word pieces and nouns like "equilibrium". No consistent token or context emerges. The circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Scattered technical-text suffixes and nouns

result.description: Fires on the token after an adjective like "keen" or "sharp" (e.g. "keen sense", "sharp kn|ives", "sharp bl|ades"). Silent on "sense" after "a" with no such adjective. Weak evidence; members mostly detect "keen" and word fragments.
result.label: Token after keen/sharp adjective

result.description: Fires on 'ulsion' in "repulsion" when it follows "minimize"/"minimizes" in electron-pairing (Hund's rule) text. It stays silent on "repulsion" in VSEPR or electron-pair-repulsion contexts.
result.label: repulsion after "minimize" (electron pairing)

result.description: Fires on the first few tokens after a sentence-opening "achieve this," (e.g. " it", " is", "fs", the next subject word), in goal-oriented business or process text. It stays silent on " is" after other purpose clauses such as "To develop characters, it is".
result.label: Token after "achieve this," clause

result.description: Fires on the 'gar' piece in "avant-garde" (weaker on the hyphen after "avant"). Members detect 'avant', the hyphen and 'gar'. Predicts the closing 'de' piece. The contrast is unrelated art text without the word.
result.label: 'gar' in avant-garde

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' the' after "like", ' processes', 'ization', sentence-initial ' The', ' choice') in dense technical or academic prose, often after a sentence boundary or garbled text. No consistent token or construction; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered academic-prose tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on ' to' (also 'mostly', 'partly') in "due to" / "thanks to" right after a statement that a field underwent significant transformation or changes. Silent on "due to" in other contexts, and on "led to" or "1800 to".
result.label: "due to" after field-change statements

result.description: Attention-layer latent peaking on scattered tokens (' participation', ' for', ' to', ' it', apostrophe-s, ' or') mid-phrase in expository text. Consistency is low and the circuit failed, so the pattern is weak and mixed.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase function words

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens (period after "Dr", word fragments, numbers) in list-like text of names and headings. It is silent on periods after full names. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered tokens in name lists

result.description: Fires on tokens in or just after "known" phrases (known as, known for, known by, also known), including the following "as"/"for"/"and"/"be". Silent on "for" in other uses like "asked for" or "basis for".
result.label: Words following "known" (known as/for)

result.description: Fires on varied tokens, mostly nouns or word pieces in cooking and kitchen text (containers, basket, edges, sticking, spoons). Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse, with no discriminative members.
result.label: Kitchen and baking nouns, diffuse

result.description: Fires on ' token' and the 'ization' piece in "tokenization" (NLP text splitting). Members are mostly ' token' detectors. Silent on general text-preprocessing text without the word.
result.label: tokenization word (token / ization)

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' to', ' methods', 'atic', 'ors', commas) within generated academic-style text about linguistics and language research. It is silent on many ' to' tokens in similar text, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Linguistics-text scattered function tokens

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' the', ' pr', 'ial', ' and', plural endings) in technical text about motion, direction, joints and orientation, often after 'and' in coordinated lists. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak and unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in motion/direction text

result.description: Fires on tokens in "as a result (of)" and similar consequence phrases (result, of after result, consequence, about), mostly right after "As a result". Silent on "of" after ordinary nouns like integration or influence.
result.label: "As a result" consequence phrases

result.description: Fires on tokens right after or at "Microsoft" (the name itself, its possessive 's, or the next product word like Windows, Power, Q). Silent on possessive apostrophes after other names. Evidence is mixed and faithfulness is weak.
result.label: Microsoft name and possessive

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ure' completing "adventure" (also 'ur' in adventurous, and similar word endings). It stays silent on 'ure' in other words like lure or nurture. Predicts travel/exploration verbs next.
result.label: 'ure' ending of "adventure"

result.description: Fires diffusely on function words (' the', ' of', ' which') and word fragments in expository text, with no consistent token or context. It stays silent on many ' the' cases. Members are generic token detectors; the evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: Diffuse function-word attention latent

result.description: Diffuse attention-layer target firing on scattered tokens: mid-word pieces, ' the', commas, 'like', in abstract expository prose. No coherent token or construction; the circuit failed faithfulness and members are generic.
result.label: Diffuse mixed tokens in expository prose

result.description: Fires on word pieces and nouns inside macroeconomic policy text about contractionary/expansionary fiscal measures (taxes, growth, -ary, measures). Silent on 'es' in business/challenges/analyses, so it needs the fiscal-policy context.
result.label: Fiscal policy text word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word right after "Aristotelian" (logic, principles, syllogistic, -ic), i.e. the noun modified by that adjective. Silent on "philosophy" after other adjectives like medieval or mathematical. Members detect Aristotle-related word pieces.
result.label: Word after "Aristotelian"

result.description: Fires on varied content words, often the second item in a contrast or list in academic or science text (climate change, Africa, dynamics, Topology, rings). There is no single dominant token, and the evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Academic content words in contrasts

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (noun/verb word pieces like "sequences", "-ize", "-ology", "has") in academic, abstract-topic text, often after linguistics, biology or science terms. Peak tokens are scattered and consistency is low; the circuit failed faithfulness, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered academic word-piece mid-phrase
'ative' in cooperative
result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ative' when it completes "cooper-ative" (cooperative vs non-cooperative models). It stays silent on 'ative' in other words like integrative, collaborative, innovative, and in some sentence-initial "Cooperative" cases.
Fires on the digit (mostly 0 or 8) in the third or fourth position of a four-digit year or range, like "19[0]0-1". It stays silent on the 0 in decade forms like "198[0]s".
result.label: Year digits in date ranges
' strateg' in business/risk contexts
result.description: Fires mostly on ' strateg' (also word pieces like 'rupt', 'ive', 'ake') in business/risk-management prose. It is silent on ' strateg' in other contexts, such as game-theory or quantitative text. The members are diffuse and unspecific.

Fires on the suffix piece 'ance'/'ances' completing "tolerance(s)", especially in engineering contexts (tolerances and fits). It stays quiet on 'ance' in other words like enhance, governance, accordance.
result.label: 'ance' ending of tolerance

result.description: Fires on the comma that ends a document-opening introductory phrase listing fields or domains ("In physics, engineering, and data science,"), just before the main clause. Silent on commas after a field name in mid-sentence or non-opening positions.
result.label: Comma closing opening field-list phrase

result.description: Fires on ' to' in the idiom "When it comes to" at the start of a document or sentence, before a topic noun or gerund. It stays silent on other uses of ' to', including mid-sentence "when it comes to" and infinitive 'to'.
result.label: "When it comes to" – 'to'

result.description: Fires on the token " section" when it starts a text, in a garbled or synthetic-looking passage with derivation/synthesis words. It stays silent on " section" after a sentence in normal prose. Members are mostly generic token detectors.
result.label: ' section' at start of odd text

result.description: Fires on the token right after or inside "Quantum" in short topic-heading lists (Quantum Decoherence, States, um, Teleportation). It is silent on "Quantum" followed by Field Theory or Entanglement in running text, so it seems to need the heading-style slot.
result.label: Quantum heading continuation tokens

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on varied tokens (' human', '-', ' the', 'ies', 'ness') mostly in text about cultures, language and human traits. Peak consistency is low and the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered culture/language-text tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, 'and', 'Object', '(', word pieces) in technical or scientific list-like text. Peaks are inconsistent and the same comma often stays silent, so there is no clear trigger or condition.
result.label: Scattered technical-text punctuation and connectives

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer latent peaking on function words and word pieces (' and', '-', ' of', ',') in academic or scientific prose, often in the middle of a list or noun phrase. Silent on many ' and' cases, and the circuit failed, so the story is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces (pher, ary, cul) of "Atmospheric ..." topic-list headings at document start, in a list of subject names. Silent on "atmospheric" in running prose. Weak, mixed evidence; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Word pieces in Atmospheric heading lists

result.description: Fires on the word after a motion verb (jumping, sweep, traveled, jump) such as a preposition or particle (off, from, into, over, on). Weak and inconsistent; the contrast shows ' off' staying silent in non-motion uses such as 'plays off' or 'seems off'.
result.label: Particle after motion verb

result.description: Diffuse, low-consistency attention circuit firing on mid-word pieces and function words (-its, -cies, -or, -ive, in) in expository text, often mid-word. Peak tokens are scattered, and the failed faithfulness means the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered mid-word and function-word peaks

result.description: Fires on plural or suffix word pieces that complete a noun (partnerhip, sponsorships, websites, plugins, pedagogical) in marketing/music/education text. Silent on 'hips' in some 'partnerships' contexts, so the cause is unclear.
result.label: Noun-completing suffix pieces (-ships, plurals)

result.description: Fires on varied tokens inside lists of innovations or techniques ("innovations like X, Y and..."), at list items, "and", or "improved" within such enumerations. Silent on "the" after "and" in abstract advancement lists. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Items in innovation/technique lists

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens (commas, 'or', 'and', 'to', mid-word pieces) in business or abstract expository prose. It is silent on many commas, and the evidence does not show a clear common trigger.
result.label: Scattered function-word and comma positions

result.description: Fires on the 'our' piece of 'flour', mostly in baking text about bread or all-purpose flour. It is weaker on 'our' in 'flourished'. Members mostly detect 'our' after 'fl'.
result.label: 'our' in flour

result.description: Fires on abstract nouns like "understanding", "analysis", "of" in abstract academic text on math/science concepts ("the concept of X, which involves the analysis..."). Peaks are scattered across tokens, and the same ' of' is silent in quantity-of phrases.
result.label: Abstract nouns in math-concept explanations

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and mid-phrase tokens (' the', ' in', ' to', ' of', occasionally content words) in expository text. The contrast silences the same ' the' in similar contexts, and members are generic, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks, unclear

result.description: Scattered peaks on unrelated tokens (' partition', '6', ' ', 'ities', ' rules', ' innov', ' be'); no consistent token or context. Members are generic token detectors with low specificity. Circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token attention latent

result.description: Fires on opening quote marks or ellipses that start the next item in a quoted list of grammar words, such as conjunctions ('and,' 'but,' 'or,'). It needs grammar-teaching text listing quoted example words. Quotes after "such as" stay silent.
result.label: Quote opening next item in grammar word list

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in lists of names, dates and items (a '1' in a year, ' and' between names, name pieces like 'rec'). No consistent token or condition; the circuit failed and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered list and name-piece tokens

result.description: Fires on the word right after a passive or copular "was/were/are" in expository text, such as the participle or adjective in "was heavily influenced" or "was slow". It stays silent on "was" itself after "it", "which" or "this".
result.label: Predicate word after was/were

result.description: Attention latent firing on varied function-like tokens (" known", " ", " his", " an", " while") in history-of-science text, often right before a noun phrase like "first known". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Mixed function tokens in science history
